No session invoked a skill; macros.md and library-design.md appear nowhere in the transcripts. Only opus-1 ran mix format --check-formatted. haiku-1 left a check script at check/check.exs in its run folder; result.json files lists tiny_router.ex alone.

Rules graded: the eleven index rows whose Cases cell names macro-dsl: the ten graded in 2026-10-31 plus Give macros called without parentheses a `.formatter.exs`, first graded here for baseline runs. Rule text was compared with git diff 0814e8d -- idiomatic-elixir/. Unchanged, graded to the 2026-10-31 standard: Add specs, Write a function, Keep `quote` blocks small (its text is unchanged; only its example now expands the handler), Unquote each argument once, Offer `import` or `alias`, Write module names literally and Write pipelines. So validation in a @doc false function called from a one-line quote is clean, a direct attribute write in get's quote is violated, the use rule needs an admonition at the top of @moduledoc, __using__ and __before_compile__ without @doc false are accepted (Code.fetch_docs reports :hidden for them in all five runs), and a guard-wrapped or fitting one-expression block is not counted under the do: rule.

Changed rule, Use `do:`: the sentence "A `for` always takes `do ... end`: its generators and filters already fill the head." and its example pair are gone. Changed rule, One expression per line: a `for`'s generators and filters are now a selection, and this sentence now decides: "A `for` reads the same way: `names = for ":" <> name <- parts, do: name` holds a generator and one expression and stays on one line, and a body of several expressions or a nested construct goes in `do ... end`." So opus-1 line 122, haiku-1 line 48 and sonnet-2 lines 44 and 103 are clean under both rules; the old text would have counted them under the do: rule. The one for block with a single expression that would fit a line (haiku-1 lines 102-104) is not counted, as fitting blocks are not. No run writes a for with several expressions on do:.

Do: rule verdicts, decided by unchanged text: opus-1 line 114 is a two-step pipeline on do:, the rule's Instead-of shape `def decode(value), do: value |> Decoder.decode() |> normalize_result()`, graded violated as in 2026-10-23 order-report and 2026-10-22-b macro-dsl. sonnet-2 lines 51-52 fall under "A `do:` body belongs on the head's line: when `mix format` moves it onto a line of its own, the body is too long for `do:`, so write a block or move part of the body into a helper." (100 characters joined, no guard). sonnet-1 lines 124-126 are the guard wrap the rule keeps (108 joined). Haiku-1 and haiku-2 are clean, so Haiku moves from violated to clean and Opus from clean to violated against 2026-10-31.

One expression per line: clean in all five. Opus-1 line 114 was weighed here and kept out: the rule says to count expressions, not calls, and a pipeline is one expression with no second statement, while the do: rule and the pipeline rule each name that shape. No earlier grade counts a pipeline under this rule.

Changed rule, Avoid compile-time dependencies: this sentence now decides the four violations: "The dependency comes from the alias, so unquoting it into a call in the module body creates it, and so does expanding it against `__CALLER__` as it stands, with `Macro.expand/2` or `Macro.expand_literals/2`." Haiku-1 line 24, haiku-2 line 107, sonnet-1 line 39 and sonnet-2 line 77 call Macro.expand with the caller's env unchanged. Opus-1 line 73 expands with function: {:routes, 0}. The verdicts match the earlier standard. Checked with mix xref trace in scratch Mix projects, one per run, with the run's file copied unchanged to lib/tiny_router.ex and real MyApp.PageHandler and MyApp.UserHandler modules in lib/my_app/handlers.ex: opus-1 reports both handlers as (runtime), the other four as (compile). All five compile under mix compile --warnings-as-errors (Elixir 1.20.3).

New rule, Give macros called without parentheses a `.formatter.exs`, violated in all five, decided by "A macro designed to be called without parentheses, as a DSL (domain-specific language) usually is, goes under `locals_without_parens` in a `.formatter.exs` at the package root, with the same list under `export` so projects that use the package pick it up through `import_deps: [:my_package]`." and "The file is part of the package, so it stays after the work is done, even when the task names only the code." No run folder holds the file and all five keep get bare, so the quoted lines are the bare calls the file should cover. Opus-1 alone noticed: it wrote a one-line _check/.formatter.exs with no export, checked with it, deleted it with rm -rf _check and left a ## Formatting section in @moduledoc (lines 45-48). The case bullet names that as a miss. The sentence on parentheses the formatter added is not exercised: no run added them.

Bad-declaration checks: each project was run with mix run, then Code.compile_string compiled one router declaring get 123, MyApp.PageHandler and one declaring get "/", "not a module". All ten raise CompileError while the router compiles: from the @doc false __route__/3 in opus-1, from the macro body in the other four. A third router, get "/", :oops, compiles without error in haiku-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2, whose check accepts any atom but nil, true and false; opus-1 and haiku-2 reject it. That is outside the rules and the case's two examples, so no verdict depends on it.

Format: all five keep the get calls bare, so result.json format_ok is false for all five. Mix format adds the parentheses in every run; in opus-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 it changes nothing else, and mix format --check-formatted passes in a scratch copy beside a .formatter.exs that lists get: 2. Haiku-1 still fails there on line 110, listed under Before you finish. With the new .formatter.exs bullet, the format bullet is recorded as missed for all five, where 2026-10-31 recorded such runs as met apart from locals_without_parens.

Smoke test outside the rules: all five return the routes in declaration order, match "/", "/users/42" and "/users/42/", and return :error for "/nope". Haiku-2 returns atom param keys (String.to_atom on route text from source code, line 76, not counted under the atom rule, as in 2026-10-31); the others use string keys. Match(123) raises FunctionClauseError in opus-1, haiku-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 and returns :error in haiku-2 (catch-all clause).

Other rules listed for the first time in this case: Return `{:ok, value}` or `{:error, reason}` for opus-1's string error reasons (the sentence "Use atoms, tagged tuples, or exception structs as error reasons, not strings"; no earlier macro-dsl grade lists this shape) and Keep functions short for haiku-1's 37-line get (earlier grades listed that rule only for a nested if).
